record.original_question: For the Kronecker sequence a_n={nα} with α irrational, let G_N be the 4-regular graph built from the first N distinct terms by connecting consecutive terms cyclically in their original order and also consecutive terms cyclically after sorting by value. Prove rigorously what large-scale structure these graphs have, and determine how that structure depends on how well α can be approximated by rationals, since the paper reports a twisted torus-like shape and says that the irrationality of α seems to matter.

evidence.quote: We will associate to them a unique 4-regular graph as follows: we connect a_i to a_{i+1} (cyclically, so a_n also gets connected to a_1). Then we order them in increasing size a_{π(1)} < a_{π(2)} < · · · < a_{π(n)} and connect a_{π(i)} to a_{π(i+1)} and conclude by also connecting to a_{π(n)} to a_{π(1)}. This results in a 4-regular graph.

The 'irrationality' of α seems to play a role (i.e. it seems to matter how well α can be approximated by rationals). We show an example for α = (1+√5)/2 in Fig. 2 where one can observe a two-dimensional object that seems to be nicely embedded in three dimensions: a torus with an additional twist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let α be an irrational number and let a_n = {nα} denote the fractional part of nα. For a positive integer N, consider the N distinct points a_1, a_2, …, a_N ∈ [0,1). Construct a 4-regular graph G_N on the vertex set {1, 2, …, N} as follows:

1. Connect i to i+1 for every 1 ≤ i ≤ N−1, and also connect N to 1 (cyclic order edges in the original index ordering).
2. Let π be the permutation of {1, …, N} such that a_{π(1)} < a_{π(2)} < ⋯ < a_{π(N)}. Connect π(i) to π(i+1) for every 1 ≤ i ≤ N−1, and also connect π(N) to π(1) (cyclic order edges in the value-sorted ordering).

The resulting multigraph is 4-regular. Numerical experiments show that, when drawn with vertices placed so as to reflect their structure, G_N appears to approximate a two-dimensional surface embedded in three-space resembling a torus with an additional twist, and that the qualitative geometric features of these graphs depend on the Diophantine approximation properties of α (e.g. its continued fraction expansion).

Problem. Prove rigorously what large-scale geometric/combinatorial structure the family {G_N}_{N ≥ 1} possesses (for instance, identify G_N as a circulant graph or a graph that admits a canonical embedding into a torus), and quantify how this structure (in particular the embedding, the genus, gap statistics, or graph-metric asymptotics) depends on the continued fraction expansion / irrationality measure of α.
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up work has made substantial progress. Using the Three-Gap Theorem, the Kronecker sequence graph G_N is known to be (for appropriate N) a circulant graph, and connected circulant graphs of this form embed into the torus, providing a combinatorial explanation of the observed torus-like shape. Further regularity results on the induced "Kronecker permutations" have appeared (e.g., Clément 2025, arXiv:2509.03782), showing that for quadratic irrationals there are infinitely many N for which the sorting permutation has cycles of length at most 4. However, a complete and quantitative rigorous description of the large-scale structure with full dependence on the Diophantine properties of α does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Finding Structure in Sequences of Real Numbers via Graph Theory: a Problem List
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list including the 4-regular Kronecker sequence graph and the observed twisted-torus structure depending on irrationality of α.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem is posed as part of a problem list, with the structure for Kronecker sequences left as a question.

status_evidence.title: Regular Structures in Kronecker Permutations (Clément, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Permutations induced by Kronecker sequences based on irrational α are extremely regular; for quadratic irrationals there are infinitely many n giving permutations whose cycles have length at most 4.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results on the sorting permutation underlying G_N have been established for Diophantine α.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces and sequence graphs (R. Green)
status_evidence.snippet: The Kronecker sequence graph is a particular circulant graph and therefore has a torus embedding; circulant graphs tesselate the torus.
status_evidence.claim: The torus-embedding structure of G_N is explained via identification with a circulant graph using the Three-Gap Theorem.
